question: Which of the following types of reaction represents formation of slaked lime from calcium oxide and water?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Combination reaction**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In a combination reaction, two or more substances combine to form a single product.
 
• The formation of slaked lime (calcium hydroxide) from calcium oxide and water is a classic example of a combination reaction.
 
• The chemical equation for this reaction is CaO + H₂O → Ca(OH)₂.
 
• This type of reaction is exothermic, meaning it releases heat.
 
• Combination reactions are also known as synthesis reactions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Decomposition reaction**

 
 
• This type of reaction involves a single compound breaking down into two or more simpler substances.
 
• An example of a decomposition reaction is the breakdown of hydrogen peroxide into water and oxygen.
 
 
 
• **Precipitation reaction**
 
 
• In a precipitation reaction, two solutions react to form an insoluble solid, known as the precipitate.
 
• An example is the reaction between silver nitrate and sodium chloride to form silver chloride precipitate.
 
 
 
• **Displacement reaction**
 
 
• This type of reaction involves an element displacing another element in a compound, forming a new compound.
 
• An example is the reaction between zinc and hydrochloric acid, where zinc displaces hydrogen to form zinc chloride and hydrogen gas.
